source.description: Reference adjustment set for the vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam vs vancomycin + cefepime AKI question. NOT transcribed from a published DAG figure. ACORN (JAMA 2023;330(16):1557-1567) is a randomized trial and publishes no DAG; the observational meta-analyses report pooled adjusted odds ratios without a shared graph. The confounder list is constructed from (a) the covariates the observational vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam AKI studies adjust for (baseline renal function, sepsis severity, nephrotoxin co-exposure, ICU status), and (b) standard reasoning about what jointly drives the choice of beta-lactam partner and measured acute kidney injury. A defensible reference for SHD/SID comparison against a generated candidate DAG, not a gold standard.
source.constructed_by: clinical reasoning + observational-emulation covariate extraction; not an author-drawn DAG
construction_notes: Every observed node is a common cause of the exposure (piperacillin-tazobactam vs cefepime as the vancomycin partner) and the outcome (measured KDIGO stage >= 2 AKI within 7 days), encoded role='confounder', temporal_classification='pre_treatment'.

MEASUREMENT-BIAS PATH, not represented as a confounder: piperacillin-tazobactam inhibits tubular secretion of creatinine, raising measured serum creatinine without a true fall in glomerular filtration rate (pseudotoxicity). This is a direct exposure -> measured-outcome path that is NOT a backdoor path and is NOT closed by any adjustment set. It is captured here only as this note and in protocol.json design_constraints, deliberately NOT as a mediator node (a mediator is part of a real total effect; this is assay interference). SHD/SID against a generated DAG should not reward or penalise a pseudotoxicity node.
Baseline serum creatinine / eGFR is the highest-weight confounder: worse baseline renal function makes some clinicians avoid piperacillin-tazobactam and is the strongest predictor of subsequent AKI.

The nephrotoxin co-exposure cluster (iodinated contrast within 72 h, NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, loop diuretics, ACE inhibitors / ARBs, calcineurin inhibitors) is collapsed into one node here for readability; protocol.json first_pass_covariates lists them separately for the actual adjustment set.
Neutropenia / haematological malignancy is a strong channelling confounder: febrile-neutropenia guidance favours cefepime, and these patients have a distinct AKI risk.
Suspected intra-abdominal source channels toward piperacillin-tazobactam (anaerobic and enterococcal cover) and independently raises AKI risk through sepsis severity and intra-abdominal hypertension.

'Institutional antibiogram / stewardship guideline' is observed=false: local resistance patterns and the written empiric-therapy pathway drive the partner choice directly and are not in the OMOP data.

'Vancomycin exposure intensity (AUC / trough)' is partially observed: higher vancomycin exposure raises AKI risk and correlates with the partner choice; trough levels exist in measurement but are sparse. Encoded observed=true with a note that coverage is incomplete.
Post-time-zero events - fluid balance after day 1, new hypotension, a second nephrotoxin started after time zero - are potential mediators and are excluded from this baseline set.

Non-fan relations: chronic kidney disease -> baseline serum creatinine / eGFR; septic shock at time zero -> vasopressor exposure at time zero; septic shock at time zero -> baseline illness-severity score.

analysis_feature_reconciliation.note: 15 observed confounder nodes (the nephrotoxin cluster is one node here, ~7 covariates in the adjustment set) + 1 unobserved. A generated candidate DAG is expected to recover baseline renal function, CKD, diabetes, sepsis severity, hypotension, and the nephrotoxin cluster at minimum; the neutropenia->cefepime channelling, the intra-abdominal-source channelling, calendar year, and the pseudotoxicity measurement path are the ones an LLM draft most often misses.

variables.label: Age at ICU admission
variables.rationale: Older patients have lower renal reserve (higher AKI risk) and a modestly different empiric-antibiotic risk profile.

variables.label: Sex
variables.rationale: Baseline demographic common cause; adjusted for in the observational vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam AKI studies.

variables.label: Baseline serum creatinine / estimated GFR
variables.rationale: The strongest single predictor of subsequent AKI and a driver of the partner choice (some clinicians avoid piperacillin-tazobactam in renal impairment).

variables.label: Chronic kidney disease
variables.rationale: Structural renal disease raises AKI susceptibility and changes prescribing caution.

variables.label: Diabetes mellitus
variables.rationale: Diabetic nephropathy and microvascular disease raise AKI risk; associated with comorbidity-driven prescribing patterns.

variables.label: Congestive heart failure
variables.rationale: Low effective circulating volume and diuretic use raise AKI risk; a common-cause comorbidity.

variables.label: Chronic liver disease / cirrhosis
variables.rationale: Hepatorenal physiology raises AKI risk; cirrhosis also influences antibiotic selection and dosing.

variables.label: Baseline illness-severity score
variables.rationale: SOFA / APACHE at time zero drives how broad the empiric regimen is and strongly predicts AKI.

variables.label: Septic shock / vasopressor exposure at time zero
variables.rationale: Shock is the dominant cause of septic AKI and prompts the broadest-spectrum empiric cover.

variables.label: Hypotension before time zero (lowest MAP in prior 24 h)
variables.rationale: Pre-antibiotic hypotension is a direct renal insult and marks the severity that drives regimen breadth.

variables.label: Nephrotoxin co-exposure cluster (contrast, NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, loop diuretics, ACEi/ARB, calcineurin inhibitors)
variables.rationale: Each raises AKI risk and correlates with the clinical context (imaging, transplant, prior therapy) that also shapes the empiric-antibiotic choice.

variables.label: Neutropenia or haematological malignancy
variables.rationale: Febrile-neutropenia guidance channels toward cefepime; these patients also have a distinct (often higher) AKI risk from chemotherapy and tumour-lysis physiology.

variables.label: Suspected intra-abdominal source of infection
variables.rationale: Anaerobic and enterococcal cover channels toward piperacillin-tazobactam; intra-abdominal sepsis independently raises AKI risk (intra-abdominal hypertension, source severity).

variables.label: Vancomycin exposure intensity (AUC or trough)
variables.rationale: Higher vancomycin exposure raises AKI risk and co-varies with the partner choice; trough data exist in measurement but coverage is incomplete.

variables.label: Calendar year of admission
variables.rationale: The vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam nephrotoxicity literature itself shifted ICU prescribing across 2015-2019; AKI ascertainment practice also changed.

variables.label: Institutional antibiogram / empiric-therapy pathway
variables.rationale: Local resistance patterns and the written empiric-antibiotic guideline drive the partner choice directly and are not represented in the OMOP data.

relations.rationale: CKD is the structural cause of the elevated baseline creatinine; the two are not independent common causes.

relations.source: Septic shock / vasopressor exposure at time zero
relations.rationale: Shock is a major determinant of the SOFA / APACHE value at time zero.
Intra-abdominal sepsis contributes to the severity score through the abdominal and haemodynamic components.
